'''Jeremy Miles Tyler''' (born June 21, 1991)<ref>{{cite web|title=Jeremy Tyler NBA & ABA Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/tylerje01.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=April 22, 2009}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Al-Rayyan SC (basketball)|Al-Arabi]] of the [[Qatari Basketball League]]. Tyler was drafted with the 39th pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] but immediately traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref name="realgm">{{cite web|title=Jeremy Tyler Player Profile – RealGM|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Jeremy_Tyler/Summary/2373|work=RealGM.com|access-date=April 22, 2009}}</ref>

==High school career==
Tyler attended [[San Diego High School]] in San Diego, California from 2006 to 2009.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Thamel |first=Pete |date=2009-04-23 |title=Basketball Prospect Leaving High School to Play in Europe |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/04/23/sports/ncaabasketball/23prospect.html |access-date=2025-01-20 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Marcus Thompson II {{!}} Bay Area News |date=2011-06-24 |title=Golden State Warriors: Second-rounder Jeremy Tyler is a most intriguing choice |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2011/06/24/golden-state-warriors-second-rounder-jeremy-tyler-is-a-most-intriguing-choice/ |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=The Mercury News |language=en-US}}</ref> As a junior in 2008–09, he averaged 28.7 points per game for the Cavers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/jeremy-tyler/RRjhCvTlEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/gendersport/basketball-stats.htm#year=08-09|title=Jeremy Tyler's High School Basketball Stats|work=MaxPreps.com|access-date=April 22, 2009}}</ref>

In April 2009, despite a commitment to the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|University of Louisville]], he chose to bypass not only college, but his senior year of high school as well.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.moneyplayersblog.com/blog/2009/04/jeremy-tyler-goes-pro-before-his-junior-prom.html|title=Jeremy Tyler goes pro before his junior prom|date=April 22, 2009|work=MoneyPlayersBlog.com|access-date=April 22, 2009}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Maccabi Haifa (2009–2010)===
In April 2009, Tyler announced his intentions to skip his senior year of high school to play professionally abroad.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/ncaa/76347/jeremy-tyler-leaving-high-school-to-play-overseas.html|title=Jeremy Tyler Leaving High School To Play Overseas|date=April 23, 2009|work=Sportando.com|access-date=April 23, 2009}}</ref> On August 23, 2009, he signed with [[Maccabi Haifa B.C.|Maccabi Haifa]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Super League|Israeli Super League]] for the 2009–10 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/78733/now-it-s-official-tyler-in-haifa.html|title=Now it's official: Tyler in Haifa|date=August 23, 2009|work=Sportando.com|access-date=August 23, 2009}}</ref>

On March 19, 2010, he parted ways with Maccabi due to personal matters and headed home to San Diego.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/80423/jeremy-tyler-leaves-maccabi-haifa.html|title=Jeremy Tyler leaves Maccabi Haifa|date=March 19, 2010|work=Sportando.com|access-date=March 19, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5008825|title=Tyler quits Maccabi with 5 weeks left|date=March 20, 2010|work=ESPN.com|access-date=March 20, 2010}}</ref> Tyler played just 10 games, averaging only 2.1 points and 1.9 rebounds in 7.6 minutes per game.

===Tokyo Apache (2010–2011)===
On July 29, 2010, Tyler signed with the [[Tokyo Apache]] of [[bj league|Japan]] for the 2010–11 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/83688/jeremy-tyler-moves-to-tokio-apache.html|title=Jeremy Tyler moves to Tokio Apache|date=July 29, 2010|work=Sportando.com|access-date=July 29, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5419379|title=Tyler to play pro ball in Japan|date=July 29, 2010|work=ESPN.com|access-date=July 29, 2010}}</ref> In 33 games, he averaged 9.9 points on 51.7% shooting and 6.4 rebounds in 15.4 minutes per game. The Apache would dissolve soon after he left due to the impact of the [[2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami|2011 earthquake and tsunami]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chinadaily.com.cn/sports/2011-05/05/content_12447824.htm|title=Japan plans basketball expansion after quake|date=May 5, 2011|work=ChinaDaily.com|access-date=November 17, 2013}}</ref>

===Golden State Warriors (2011–2013)===
Tyler was selected with the 39th overall pick by the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]] in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. His rights were later traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] for cash considerations on draft night. On December 13, 2011, he signed with the Warriors.<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors Sign Rookies Klay Thompson & Jeremy Tyler|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_sign_thompson_tyler_121311.html|access-date=December 13, 2011|work=NBA.com|date=December 13, 2011}}</ref> On February 27, 2012, he was assigned to the [[Dakota Wizards]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors Assign Jeremy Tyler To The Dakota Wizards|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/santacruz/jereymy_tyler_assigned_to_wizards_022712.html|access-date=February 27, 2012|work=NBA.com|date=February 27, 2012}}</ref> and recalled on March 6.<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors Recall Jeremy Tyler From The Dakota Wizards|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_recall_jeremy_tyler_030612.html|access-date=March 6, 2012|work=NBA.com|date=March 6, 2012}}</ref> For most of his rookie year he received minimal playing time, but on March 21, in a game against the New Orleans Hornets, he was named the Warriors' starting center. He subsequently remained in the team's starting line-up for the rest of the season.

In July 2012, Tyler joined the Warriors for the 2012 NBA Summer League. During his second season, he had multiple assignments with the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=2012–13 NBA Assignments |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |access-date=February 21, 2013 |work=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327190108/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |archive-date=March 27, 2014 }}</ref>

On February 21, 2013, Tyler was traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for a future second-round pick<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors Trade Jeremy Tyler to Atlanta|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/tyler_trade_022113|access-date=February 21, 2013|work=NBA.com|date=February 21, 2013}}</ref> and waived on March 6 by the Hawks after appearing in just one game.<ref>{{cite news|title=HAWKS WAIVE JEREMY TYLER|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-waive-jeremy-tyler|access-date=March 6, 2013|work=NBA.com|date=March 6, 2013}}</ref>

===Santa Cruz Warriors (2013)===
On March 18, 2013, Tyler was acquired by the Santa Cruz Warriors<ref>{{cite news|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Acquire Jeremy Tyler|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/santacruz/warriors_acquire_tyler.html|access-date=March 18, 2013|work=NBA.com|date=March 18, 2013}}</ref> as he played out the rest of the 2012–13 season in the D-League.

In July 2013, Tyler joined the New York Knicks for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On August 6, 2013, he signed with the Knicks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13981|title=New York Knicks sign Jeremy Tyler|work=InsideHoops.com|date=August 6, 2013|access-date=August 6, 2015}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Knicks on October 25, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14639|title=Knicks waive Ike Diogu, C.J. Leslie, Josh Powell, Jeremy Tyler, Chris Douglas-Roberts|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 25, 2013|access-date=October 25, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029184157/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14639|archive-date=October 29, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

After being reacquired by the Santa Cruz Warriors on November 1, 2013, three days later, Tyler was traded to the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]].<ref name="realgm" /><ref>{{cite news|title=The Erie BayHawks acquired the rights to Jeremy Tyler|url=http://www.postingandtoasting.com/2013/11/4/5066276/the-erie-bayhawks-acquired-the-rights-to-jeremy-tyler|access-date=November 4, 2013|work=PostingAnd Toasting.com|date=November 4, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=BayHawks Complete Training Camp Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/TrainingCampRoster.html|access-date=November 1, 2013|work=NBA.com|date=November 1, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151007060747/http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/TrainingCampRoster.html|archive-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref>

=== New York Knicks (2013–2014) ===
On December 31, 2013, he re-signed with the Knicks.<ref>{{cite news|title=Knicks waive Chris Smith|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/10216491/new-york-knicks-waive-chris-smith-add-jeremy-tyler|access-date=December 31, 2013|work=ESPN.com|date=December 31, 2013}}</ref> On January 28, 2014, he recorded a career-high 17 points, along with 5 rebounds and 2 blocks, in a 114–88 victory over the Boston Celtics.<ref>{{cite news|title=Notebook: Knicks 114, Celtics 88|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140128/BOSNYK/gameinfo.html|access-date=January 28, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302153509/http://www.nba.com/games/20140128/BOSNYK/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 2, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 29, he was assigned to the Erie BayHawks,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15145|title=Knicks assign Cole Aldrich, Toure Murry, Jeremy Tyler to D-League|access-date=September 25, 2015|date=January 29, 2014|work=InsideHoops.com}}</ref> only to be recalled the next day.<ref>{{cite news|title=Knicks Recall Three Players from Erie|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4733730|access-date=January 30, 2014|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=January 30, 2014}}</ref>

In July 2014, Tyler re-joined the Knicks for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]]. On August 6, 2014, he was traded, along with [[Wayne Ellington]] and a 2016 second-round pick, to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for [[Quincy Acy]] and [[Travis Outlaw]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/blog/kings-acquire-jeremy-tyler-wayne-ellington-and-2016-second-round-draft-considerations-trade-new-york|title=Kings Acquire Jeremy Tyler, Wayne Ellington and 2016 Second-Round Draft Considerations in Trade with New York|date=August 6, 2014|work=NBA.com|access-date=August 6, 2014}}</ref> On September 6, 2014, he was waived by the Kings.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kings Waive Jeremy Tyler|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-waive-jeremy-tyler|access-date=September 6, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=September 6, 2014}}</ref>

On September 23, 2014, he signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Lakers Sign Four to Training Camp Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140923four_signed_trainingcamp|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=September 23, 2014}}</ref> but was waived on October 20.<ref>{{cite news|title=Lakers Waive Appling and Tyler|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/141020lakers_wavie_appling_tyler|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2014}}</ref>

===Shanxi Zhongyu (2014–2015)===
On October 25, 2014, Tyler signed with [[Shanxi Zhongyu]] for the [[2014–15 CBA season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/138795/shanxi-zhongyu-sign-jeremy-tyler.html|title=Shanxi Zhongyu sign Jeremy Tyler|work=Sportando.com|date=October 25, 2014|access-date=October 25, 2014}}</ref> In 41 games for Shanxi, he averaged 22.1 points, 11.2 rebounds, 1.2 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.3 blocks per game.

=== Houston Rockets (2015) ===
In July 2015, Tyler joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]] where he averaged 11.8 points, 8.3 rebounds and 1.2 steals in six games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2015/players/sl_jeremy_tyler/|title=2015 Summer League Player Profile – Jeremy Tyler|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 29, 2015}}</ref> On September 28, 2015, he signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Heinrich|first=Garret|url=http://houston.cbslocal.com/2015/09/28/houston-rockets-announce-training-camp-roster/|title=Houston Rockets Announce Training Camp Roster|work=CBS.com|date=September 28, 2015|access-date=September 29, 2015}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Rockets on October 23 after appearing in two preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/HoustonRockets/status/657595154300141568|title=Rockets announced today that the team has...|work=Twitter|date=October 23, 2015|access-date=October 23, 2015}}</ref>

=== Fujian Sturgeons (2015–2016) ===
On November 25, he returned to China, this time signing with the [[Fujian Sturgeons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2015-11/25/c_134854035.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208113921/http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2015-11/25/c_134854035.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 8, 2015|title=Ex-NBA player Tyler joins China's Fujian SBS|work=XinhuaNet.com|date=November 25, 2015|access-date=December 6, 2015}}</ref> He made his debut for the team later that day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2015/1125_1980_5081.asp|title=Regular Season Round 9: Sichuan BW – Fujian QB 128–101|work=Eurobasket.com|date=November 25, 2015|access-date=December 6, 2015}}</ref>

=== Tianjin Ronggang (2016–2017) ===
On September 22, 2016, Tyler signed with [[Tianjin Ronggang]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/463722/Jeremy-Tyler-is-a-newcomer-at-TianJin-Steel|title=Jeremy Tyler is a newcomer at TianJin Steel|work=Asia-Basket.com|date=September 22, 2016|access-date=October 2, 2016}}</ref>

===Sydney Kings (2017–2018)===
On November 9, 2017, Tyler signed with the [[Sydney Kings]] for the rest of the [[2017–18 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sydneykings.com/news/article/35842-kings-sign-american-centre-jeremy-tyler|title=Kings sign American centre Jeremy Tyler|work=SydneyKings.com|date=November 9, 2017|access-date=November 9, 2017|archive-date=November 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171109134716/http://www.sydneykings.com/news/article/35842-kings-sign-american-centre-jeremy-tyler|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 9, 2018, he was released by the Kings.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jeremy Tyler released|url=http://www.sydneykings.com/news/article/36294-jeremy-tyler-released|access-date=January 9, 2018|work=SydneyKings.com|date=January 9, 2018}}</ref> In 11 games, he averaged 13.3 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.1 blocks per game.

===TNT KaTropa (2018)===
In March 2018, Tyler signed with the [[TNT KaTropa]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] as their import for the [[2018 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/news/tnt-katropa-bank|title=TNT banking on former prep-to-pro cager Jeremy Tyler as Commissioner's Cup import |first=Gerry|last=Ramos|date=March 23, 2018}}</ref>

=== Atléticos de San Germán (2019) ===
Tyler played for [[Atléticos de San Germán]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] league during the 2019–20 season.

===Liaoning Flying Leopards (2021)===
In April 2021, [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]] announced the signing of Tyler.<ref>{{cite web|title=泰勒昨日完成注册 将身披4号战袍代表辽篮征战CBA联赛|url=https://weibo.com/3610389144/Kankg3Jet|website=weibo.com|publisher=Liaoning Flying Leopards on Sina Weibo|date=April 11, 2021|access-date=April 12, 2021|trans-title=Tyler finished his registration yesterday, to play for Liaoning as No.4}}</ref>

===Wisconsin Herd (2024)===
On March 1, 2024, Tyler joined the [[Wisconsin Herd]],<ref>{{cite web|title=WISCONSIN HERD ADDS JEREMY TYLER|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-adds-jeremy-tyler|website=NBA.com|date=March 1, 2024|access-date=March 1, 2024}}</ref> but was waived on March 18.<ref>{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Wisconsin Herd Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Wisconsin-Herd/50/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 18, 2024}}</ref>

===South Bay Lakers (2024)===
On March 21, 2024, Tyler joined the [[South Bay Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2023-2024 South Bay Lakers Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/South-Bay-Lakers/12/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 22, 2024}}</ref>

===Return to Quebradillas (2024)===
On April 15, 2024, Tyler re-signed with the [[Piratas de Quebradillas]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=La Guerra del BSN|title=#BSNPR {{¡}} OFICIAL: El centro Jeremy Tyler regresa como refuerzo de los Piratas de Quebradillas en sustitución de Chris Silva quien sufrió una lesión. Tyler ya se encuentra en Puerto Rico y se reportó al equipo. El centro promedió 13.3 PPJ y 6.4 RPJ en 21.6 minutos por partido en su última actuación con los Indios de Mayagüez. 📝 @gabyquile {{¡}} @VoceroPR|number=1779907680162709974|user=LaGuerraBSN|date=April 15, 2024|access-date=April 15, 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Central Club (2025–present)===
On January 3, 2025, Tyler signed with the [[Club Central Jounieh|Central Club]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Centrale inks Jeremy Tyler, ex Quebradillas |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/news/910204/Centrale-inks-Jeremy-Tyler-ex-Quebradillas |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=January 4, 2025 |date=January 3, 2025}}</ref>
